title: Pre-meeting brief: Snowflake

tldr.text: Snowflake unveiled Cortex AI Gateway and new AI agent features (CoCo, CoWork, Marketplace) to help enterprises govern and scale AI workloads.
The company deepened its Oracle partnership, planning a native Snowflake AI Data Cloud service on OCI.

keyDevelopments.text: Snowflake added CoCo mode in Snowsight, Cloud Agents for autonomous coding, CoWork Profiles, and an Agentic Marketplace for conversational data sourcing.
Snowflake launched Cortex AI Gateway, letting enterprises such as Glean and Kargo scale AI agents while preserving security, compliance, and spend controls.
Partner Uniphore extends Cortex AI Gateway controls to the agents it orchestrates for joint customers.
USA Cycling selected Snowflake to support its LA28 race strategy.

sources.title: Snowflake Helps Enterprises Deploy Trusted AI Agents
sources.snippet: Enterprises including Glean and Kargo are already using Cortex AI Gateway to scale AI agents across their business without losing control of security, compliance, or spend. Partners including Uniphore extend Cortex AI Gateway controls to the agents they orchestrate for joint customers. [...] Detect agent overreach and insider misuse before it becomes an incident: Cortex AI Gateway's Agent Abuse Detection4analyzes complete agent trajectories, not individual prompts, to catch agents operating beyond their permissions and employees using agents to bypass approvals or exfiltrate sensitive data. A two-stage engine pairs efficient screening with context-aware reasoning, so security teams receive explainable findings instead of alert noise. Snowflake also served as a technical design partner with OpenAI on Private Safety Processing (PSP)5 which will enrich dangerous agent activity detection analysis with privacy-preserving safety signals from OpenAI and improve its effectiveness. [...] “Enterprises don’t just need more agents. They need to industrialize AI across the business. Snowflake gives our joint customers a governed data foundation,” said Frank Petterson, Chief Product and Technology Officer, Uniphore. "Uniphore's zero-copy Data & AI Orchestration Platform gives the customer the ability to autonomously create the data ontology, fine-tune SLMs and build agents while data stays in-place, and governance carries through to every agent we deploy. Cortex AI Gateway keeps that model

SNOWFLAKE EXPEDITION 2026 – Nov. 3, 2026 – Snowflake (NYSE: SNOW), the AI Data Cloud company, today at Snowflake Expedition 2026 announced new innovations that put context, security, and governance at the foundation of every AI agent, not bolted on after the fact. Snowflake is interoperable by design, connecting an organization's entire data estate across catalogs and clouds, providing the universal governance controls and context that agents and analytics depend on. To bring that same governance and context to autonomous agents, Snowflake is bringing new capabilities to Horizon Context, the home for governed business context inside Snowflake Horizon Catalog. Snowflake’s new Business Ontology3 allows these agents to operate with a shared, pre-approved understanding of core business definitions to enable reliable answers. While Cortex AI Gateway1 governs how the agents access models, invoke tools, and take action across enterprise systems. As a result, every decision and operation remains secure, fully auditable, and bound to a single set of policies, on a single data copy, regardless of which cloud, catalog, or engine the data sits in. Trusted and reliable agents are hard to build. Not because of model limitations, but because enterprise context is inherently fractured. According to a recent MIT Technology Review Insights report sponsored by Snowflake, 55% of executives cite a lack of business context as the primary cause of low-quality AI agent insights, with fragmented or inaccessible data ranking second at 45%.". As these agents spread across the business, connecting to models, MCP servers, and enterprise systems, they’re multiplying faster than IT and security can keep up. Companies are left with an impossible choice between scaling AI quickly while absorbing inaccuracies, vulnerabilities, and runaway costs, and slamming the brakes on the very momentum they are trying to build. Snowflake eliminates that tradeoff by giving organizations the confidence to move fast without losing control. With shared business context grounded in an organization’s entire data estate, active execution guardrails, and unified policies governed across every cloud and engine, teams no longer have to choose between agent velocity and enterprise security. The agentic enterprise runs on more than data access, it runs on data companies can govern, agents they can control, and answers they can trust. Snowflake Inc (SNOW) moved up by 3.07%. The Software & IT Services sector is up by 0.71%. The company outperformed the industry. Top 3 stocks by turnover in the sector: Microsoft Corp (MSFT) down 2.35%; CoreWeave Inc (CRWV) up 23.72%; Meta Platforms Inc (META) down 0.91%. What is driving Snowflake Inc (SNOW)’s stock price up today? Snowflake demonstrated solid upward momentum and heightened intraday trading activity as enterprise software sentiment strengthened and investors revisited high-quality cloud data infrastructure assets. Following recent consolidation across the broader infrastructure software cohort, market participants stepped in to absorb recent selling pressure, driven by renewed confidence in consumption-oriented data and artificial intelligence workloads. A primary catalyst supporting the advance is sustained institutional optimism regarding Snowflake's evolving artificial intelligence product roadmap. The rapid enterprise adoption of first-party agentic tools, such as Cortex AI, CoCo, and CoWork, alongside deeper integration across major hyperscale environments like Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, has reinforced the platform's positioning as foundational infrastructure for corporate generative AI deployment. Positive sell-side sentiment has amplified this narrative, with recent research notes reiterating constructive ratings and highlighting robust net revenue retention trends, suggesting that core platform utilization remains resilient despite broader enterprise cost governance. Additionally, technical dynamics and positioning ahead of the upcoming fiscal third-quarter earnings cycle played a key role in today's price action. After testing key technical support levels earlier in the week, buying interest accelerated as algorithmic and fundamental accounts recognized a favorable risk-reward setup. Market participants also effectively looked past routine scheduled insider divestitures filed under Rule 10b5-1 trading plans, treating them as programmatic liquidity events rather than fundamental inflection points. While the broader macroeconomic landscape continues to present valuation sensitivity due to elevated forward revenue multiples, the current session underscores strong dip-buying demand for mission-critical enterprise cloud architectures. In the near term, institutional focus will remain squarely on forward product revenue guidance, enterprise consumption trajectory, and gross margin evolution within AI-heavy compute workloads. sources.content: Skip to content Blog/Product and Technology/Build Faster and Work Smarter with AI Agents and Apps Grounded in Data Nov 3, 2026/9 min readProduct and Technology Build Faster and Work Smarter with AI Agents and Apps Grounded in Data Arun Agarwal Arun Agarwal +2 Image of Expedition mountain icon Only 11% of organizations have agents in production despite 38% piloting them, according to Deloitte's 2026 Tech Trends report. We see this gap between pilots and production deployments happening across industries and companies of all sizes: Teams build a compelling demo and deploy it against real data, only to have it confidently return the wrong revenue number or miss a policy constraint that a junior analyst would have caught. The problem is a lack of context. Agents need to know which metric definition is authoritative, which data is current, what permissions each user holds and what happened in the last conversation. Without that grounding, even the most capable model operates on guesswork. And even when agents get the answer right, it can be difficult to share those insights with the rest of the business. At Expedition 2026, Snowflake is announcing capabilities across three dimensions that strengthen how agents and apps run alongside your data, with full governance and context: Ground: Connect agents to your governed data, metrics and business logic so they answer questions from authoritative definitions, not guesswork. Act: Allow agents to execute real work following each user's own permissions, in the tools teams already use, with clear auditability. Quickly and securely ship Snowflake apps on governed data so people and agents can extract insights and take action. Compound: Share proven skills, profiles and memory across the organization so every new agent starts off better than the last. Ground: Give every agent relevant data and business context from Day 1 The a16z research team put it plainly in their March 2026 analysis: "A crucial reason agents didn’t work well was a lack of proper data context." An agent answering the question "What was revenue growth last quarter?" can write competent SQL against a plausible-looking table yet return wrong numbers with full confidence because nobody told it which field carries the authoritative definition of “revenue.” Snowflake's approach starts from the principle that agents should inherit the context your organization has already built: the schemas, metrics, business logic, governance policies and permissions that define how your data works. Several new and enhanced capabilities make this practical. Snowflake Cortex Sense (public preview soon) autobuilds context from your existing schemas, metric definitions and business logic, so you don’t spend weeks setting up and defining connections. Cortex Sense works across your own data, shared data and data you purchase through Snowflake Marketplace — so agents understand the entire picture, not just one team's slice of it. When agents need to reason over large volumes of unstructured information, Analytical Search (public preview) lets them count, compare and find trends across thousands of documents at once, from contracts and support tickets to internal reports. This is not keyword search; Analytical Search applies AI functions across document collections to answer questions such as "How many contracts contain a price escalation clause?" or "Which support tickets mention the same root cause?" And because Cortex Search now enforces row access and masking policies on source tables (private preview), the documents an agent can see follow the same rules as the structured data it queries. As agents move from finding documents to understanding them, Snowflake’s new embedding model Arctic Embed 3S (generally available soon) improves retrieval quality over Arctic Embed L-v2.0 by 3% in English, 6% in multilingual retrieval, and 23% for structured tables and columns, while keeping the same compact size class. sources.title: Snowflake and Oracle: Bringing the AI Data Cloud to OCI
sources.snippet: Christian Kleinerman Christian Kleinerman Snowflake and Oracle are announcing the expansion of their partnership with Snowflake on OCI. When available, Snowflake on OCI will be a native, first-party offering that brings Snowflake's AI Data Cloud to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). The offering would bring Snowflake's capabilities across AI, analytics, data engineering and transactions, as well as applications and collaboration, closer to enterprise data in Oracle databases, applications and OCI services, with purchasing and billing directly through Oracle. [...] ## Integrated connectivity to Oracle applications and databases It matters where customers process data, particularly when operational and analytical systems exchange information frequently. Customers already connect Oracle data sources to Snowflake today through native and partner connectors. This partnership expands on that strong foundation. The planned offering would use native integrations to bring data from supported Oracle applications and databases into Snowflake on OCI, reducing the need for custom pipelines and accelerating the use of that data for analytics and AI. [...] For Oracle customers, the opportunity extends beyond adding another platform to their environment.
